source_title: See 10 Vintage Photos of a Young Patrick Stewart During His Early Career - People.com
source_excerpt:
The star of ‘Star Trek’ and ‘X-Men’ died on Oct. 28 after being diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia
Malcolm McNeill/Mirrorpix/Getty; Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty
Patrick Stewart was destined to become a performer.
The late English actor developed a passion for drama when he was introduced to the works of William Shakespeare at 12 years old by an English teacher, according to an essay he wrote for The Guardian in October 2021. Stewart eventually went on to build a robust career in theater, film and television. Most famously, he depicted Captain Picard in the Star Trek franchise and Professor X in the X-Men films .
“ He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise,” Kelly Bush Novak, Stewart’s longtime spokesperson, wrote in an October statement.
The statement continued, “He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life.”
Stewart died on Oct. 28 at 86 years old. He had previously been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.
Here’s a look back at several vintage photos of Patrick Stewart during the early days of his career.
In a 1970 production of Shakespeare’s play The Two Gentlemen of Verona , Stewart starred as Launce and worked with a sweet scene partner: a rescue dog named Blackie, who played his character’s trusty pet Crab.
Among Stewart’s early roles was a part in the BBC’s historical drama miniseries I, Claudius . Released in 1976, the series featured Stewart as Sejanus, who plotted against Tiberius during his reign. Here, he acted alongside Patricia Quinn , who played Nero’s daughter Livilla.
Stewart developed many longstanding professional relationships in his decades-long career, including with actress Janet Suzman, with whom he appeared in productions like the 1974 movie Antony and Cleopatra . Here, they posed during Suzman’s birthday party in 1979.
Stewart posed for several portraits and red carpet moments over the years. This photo taken in March 1982 is among many with him sporting a genuine, infectious smile.
Stewart continued to steal scenes in his early career, including in the 1986 film Lady Jane . He starred as Henry Grey, Duke of Suffolk and father to Helena Bonham Carter ’s Lady Jane Grey.
In 1988, Stewart posed for a portrait while wearing a soft white sweater in Los Angeles.
Stewart was locked into character as Captain Picard when this snapshot was taken in 1987 on set for Star Trek: The Next Generation at Paramount Studios in Hollywood, Calif.
Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty
Stewart spent time at the theater on and offstage. Here, he dressed up to attend the Center Theatre Group’s A Lie of the Mind play during the show’s opening night on Jan. 21, 1988, in L.A.
While at Dodger Stadium in April 1990, Stewart was captured under the glow of the L.A. sun.
Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty
Stewart donned a casual ensemble in September 1990 outside of the Pasadena Civic Auditorium, where he attended rehearsals to present during the 42nd Annual Primetime Emmy Awards that year.
